## Go-Live Readiness: bande-ops on real Amazon data

### 1. Summary

Not close. The plumbing is sound — host routing, LWA token exchange, retry/backoff, the server-only/credentials-never-reach-browser boundary, the synced-mirror architecture, and (correctly) the *absence* of AWS SigV4/STS AssumeRole, which Amazon removed in 2023-24. But every one of the three integrations has at least one hard blocker that will either 400 on the first real call or, worse, silently return wrong data. SP-API catalog SKU lookups fail without a `sellerId` we don't yet configure; inventory quantities come back empty because `details=true` is missing, collapsing every SKU to UNKNOWN; the Reorder demand provider is a throw-only skeleton wired in an architecturally wrong shape (per-SKU at page load vs. one batched async report); and the Advertising client targets a Sponsored Products v2 endpoint Amazon **sunset on 2023-03-30**. The dangerous failures aren't the 400s (loud, easy to catch) — they're the three places where the project's central UNKNOWN-vs-true-0 invariant silently breaks once real data flows. Plan on real implementation work in all three modules plus a credentials/sandbox flip, not a config toggle.

### 1a. 2026-07-21 live inventory reorder update

The `feat/live-inventory-reorder` branch addresses the reorder-specific blockers from this audit:

- SP-API catalog SKU lookups now carry `SPAPI_SELLER_ID` for live SKU search.
- FBA inventory requests use detailed inventory and persist fulfillable plus inbound buckets.
- Catalog, FBA inventory, and AWD inventory paginate.
- AWD inventory is stored as its own synced mirror.
- FBA ledger velocity is now a scheduled mirror using one report per marketplace/window, not per-SKU page-load calls.
- Report document download uses the presigned document URL separately from SP-API JSON requests.
- Reorder recommendations read persisted FBA, AWD, SVD, source mappings, sales velocity, policy, and freshness state.
- SVD inventory refresh is owner-triggered from the Reorder page and uses server-side `SVD_USERNAME`/`SVD_PASSWORD`.

Remaining go-live checks: apply migration `0010`, provide live Amazon and SVD env vars, verify the new SP-API/AWD/ledger/SVD paths against real credentials, and still migrate Advertising API to Sponsored Products v3 before trusting Ads live data.

### 2. Per-integration changes

#### SP-API — Catalog & Inventory (`lib/amazon/`)

Ordered by severity.

1. **[BLOCKER] Catalog SKU lookup omits required `sellerId`.** `client.ts:143-160` (`listCatalogItems`) sets `identifiersType: 'SKU'` and `identifiers: opts.sellerSkus` but never sends `sellerId`. Per Catalog Items v2022-04-01 (`GET /catalog/2022-04-01/items`, `searchCatalogItems`), `sellerId` is **required whenever `identifiersType=SKU`** (SKUs are seller-scoped); omitting it returns HTTP 400 InvalidInput. `config.ts` has no seller-id field — `REQUIRED_ENV` is only `LWA_CLIENT_ID`/`LWA_CLIENT_SECRET`/`SPAPI_REFRESH_TOKEN`. Add a `SELLER_ID` (merchant token) env var to `AmazonConfig` and thread it into the query whenever `sellerSkus` is supplied. (Confirmed against official docs and the amzn/selling-partner-api-models OpenAPI.)

2. **[BLOCKER — silent data corruption] Inventory `details=true` missing → every SKU reads UNKNOWN.** `client.ts:167-176` (`getInventorySummaries`) sends `{ granularityType, granularityId, marketplaceIds, sellerSkus }` with no `details` param. `GET /fba/inventory/v1/summaries` returns `totalQuantity`/`inventoryDetails` **only when `details=true`**; the default (`details=false`) returns summaries with no quantities. So `raw.totalQuantity` is `undefined` → `toQuantity` → `null`, and every SKU is mislabeled UNKNOWN. This directly violates the UNKNOWN-vs-0 invariant the project treats as core (`types.ts`, CLAUDE.md "Do Not"). It doesn't error — it poisons the data — which is why it's a blocker, not a medium. Add `details: 'true'`.

3. **[HIGH] Mapped `CatalogItem.sku` is always `''`.** `client.ts:217-223` derives sku by scanning `raw.identifiers` for `identifierType === 'SKU'`. Catalog Items v2022-04-01 `identifiers` returns only external/global identifiers (UPC, EAN, GTIN, ISBN, JAN, MINSAN) per marketplace — the seller SKU is a **request-only** search parameter and is never echoed in the response body. So the `find()` never matches and sku is `''` for every item. Carry the SKU from the request input (`opts.sellerSkus`, which the code already has and discards) or source it from the Listings Items API / `GET_MERCHANT_LISTINGS` report. (Confirmed by code read + official docs.)

4. **[MEDIUM] Pagination ignored on both APIs (silent truncation).** `CatalogItemsResponse` models only `{ items }` and `InventorySummariesResponse` only `{ payload.inventorySummaries }`. `searchCatalogItems` returns `pagination.nextToken` with default pageSize 10 (max 20); `getInventorySummaries` returns a sibling `pagination.nextToken`. Without a nextToken loop (`pageToken` query param on catalog) the client returns at most the first page.

5. **[MEDIUM] Sandbox-first default serves canned fixtures, not real data.** `config.ts:28-32` defaults `AMAZON_USE_SANDBOX` to `'true'`, resolving to `marketplace.sandboxHost`. SP-API sandbox returns static mock responses keyed to each operation's `x-amzn-api-sandbox` definition — never the seller's real catalog/inventory. Must set `AMAZON_USE_SANDBOX=false` (prod host `sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com`). Host strings themselves are correct.

6. **[MEDIUM] Rate-limit headers not honored.** `client.ts` retries 429/5xx with jittered exponential backoff but ignores `Retry-After` and `x-amzn-RateLimit-Limit`. FBA `getInventorySummaries` is 2 rps (burst 2); catalog is 5 rps. Blind backoff works but risks sustained 429s under batch syncs — honor the dynamic headers and add a proactive throttle.

7. **[POLISH] Superfluous `Authorization: Bearer`.** `client.ts:103-104` sends both `authorization: Bearer <token>` and `x-amz-access-token: <token>`. SP-API authenticates solely via `x-amz-access-token`; the Bearer header is ignored — harmless but non-spec.

8. **[POLISH] No User-Agent; unfiltered marketplace/image selection.** No `User-Agent` header (SP-API recommends `AppName/Version`). `mapCatalogItem` takes `summaries[0]` and `images[0].images[0]` without filtering by `marketplaceId` or preferring `variant === 'MAIN'`, so it can grab the wrong marketplace or a non-MAIN image.

Affirmed correct: omission of SigV4/STS AssumeRole, prod/sandbox host strings, and the LWA endpoint.

#### Reorder demand — FBA ledger (`lib/reorder/spapi-demand.ts`)

`spapi-demand.ts` is an explicit throw-only skeleton (`getDailyDemand` throws "not implemented"). Every gap below is unbuilt, not buggy; the documented intent (PII-free aggregate movements, no Restricted Data Token) is correct.

1. **[BLOCKER — architecture] Per-SKU seam vs. one batched async report.** `demand.ts` defines `getDailyDemand(sku, marketplaceId)` one SKU at a time, and `service.ts:124-148` calls it inside `catalogRows.map(async …)` wrapped in `Promise.all` — once per catalog SKU at page-render time. But `createReport` (`POST /reports/2021-06-30/reports`) for `GET_LEDGER_SUMMARY_VIEW_DATA` is rate-limited to ~0.0167 req/s (~1/min, burst 15) and the report takes minutes to reach `processingStatus: DONE`. The report already contains every MSKU for the window in one document. The current shape invites N createReport calls and a multi-minute page hang. Correct design: ONE report per marketplace+window on a cron/sync path (like `inventory_levels`), parsed once into a SKU→daily-demand map, persisted as a synced mirror — not an on-demand per-SKU call at page load.

2. **[BLOCKER — missing primitive] Report-document download (presigned S3, gzipped TSV, no auth header).** The only HTTP primitive is `SpApiClient.request()`, which always sends `authorization` + `x-amz-access-token` and parses JSON. The report document is fetched from a **presigned S3 URL with no SP-API auth header**, is **gzip-compressed TSV**, not JSON. A separate download/decompress primitive is required; the existing client cannot do it.

3. **[MEDIUM — correctness] Field, grouping, and polling details.** The demand column is "Customer shipments," not "units shipped." `DAILY` `reportOptions`, Disposition/Location row grouping, and sign handling are unaddressed. Polling must handle terminal `FATAL`/`CANCELLED` states, not just `DONE`. Ledger MSKUs can be truncated/variant forms and must be reconciled back to the canonical catalog SKU before summing (noted in the file's JSDoc, deferred to this provider).

Affirmed correct: PII-free aggregate approach, no RDT, and the "null = UNKNOWN, never 0" contract the skeleton's throw preserves.

#### Advertising API — Sponsored Products (`lib/ads/`)

This module was not in the provided audit; findings below are from a direct code read + verification against Amazon's current docs.

1. **[BLOCKER] Target endpoint `/v2/sp/campaigns` is sunset.** `client.ts:214-221` issues `GET /v2/sp/campaigns`. Sponsored Products **v2 was deprecated on 2023-03-30** and the endpoint no longer exists. Migrate to SP v3: `POST /sp/campaigns/list` with `Content-Type` and `Accept: application/vnd.spCampaign.v3+json`, a JSON body (e.g. `stateFilter`), pagination via `nextToken`/`maxResults`.

2. **[BLOCKER, couples to #1] v3 is POST returning an object, not a GET returning an array.** `request<RawCampaign[]>` expects a flat array; v3 returns `{ campaigns: [...], nextToken }`. `listCampaigns` and the response typing both break against real v3.

3. **[HIGH] Budget field shape changed → every `daily_budget` reads UNKNOWN.** `RawCampaign.dailyBudget` (`client.ts:230`, mapped at `:238`) is the v2 top-level field. v3 nests it under a `budget` object (`budget.budget`, `budgetType`). On real v3 data `raw.dailyBudget` is `undefined` → `toBudget` → `null`, so every campaign's `daily_budget` is UNKNOWN — same invariant break as the inventory bug. Read the nested v3 budget.

4. **[HIGH] State enum case mismatch → every campaign mislabeled `paused`.** `toCampaignState` (`client.ts:84-88`) matches lowercase `'enabled'`/`'archived'` (v2 values) and defaults everything else to `'paused'`. v3 returns uppercase `ENABLED`/`PAUSED`/`ARCHIVED`, so on real v3 data every campaign silently collapses to `paused`. The "default unknown to the non-spending state" instinct is sound; the matched values are version-wrong.

5. **[MEDIUM] Pagination ignored.** No `nextToken`/`maxResults` handling — same truncation risk as SP-API.

6. **[MEDIUM] Sandbox-first default.** `config.ts:39-51` defaults `ADS_USE_SANDBOX`/`AMAZON_USE_SANDBOX` to `'true'` (`advertising-api-test.amazon.com`, canned data). Set to `false` for prod (`advertising-api.amazon.com`).

Affirmed correct (and notably different from SP-API): the Advertising API **does** use `Authorization: Bearer <LWA token>`, so the Bearer header here is correct, not superfluous. The `Amazon-Advertising-API-ClientId` + `Amazon-Advertising-API-Scope` (profile id) headers, the NA prod/sandbox hosts, and the separate-LWA-creds/profile model are all right.

### 3. Security & correctness findings

- **The UNKNOWN-vs-0 invariant silently breaks in two live data paths today and would in a third.** Inventory `totalQuantity` (missing `details=true`) and Ads `daily_budget` (wrong v3 field) both resolve to `null`/UNKNOWN for every row without erroring. This is the most dangerous failure class here: the app looks healthy and feeds wrong numbers into reorder math and ad views. Treat both as correctness blockers, not polish.
- **Sandbox-first defaults are an ops footgun.** Both `config.ts` files default the sandbox flag to `true`. A forgotten env flip means production silently serves Amazon's canned fixtures while appearing live. Consider defaulting to prod and opting *into* sandbox, or a startup assertion that fails loud if sandbox is on outside dev.
- **SP-API `Authorization: Bearer` carries the LWA access token to a header SP-API ignores.** Low risk (same host, TLS), but it's an access token in an unexpected header — drop it.
- **No `User-Agent`.** Amazon recommends a descriptive UA; unidentified clients risk deprioritization/throttling. Low.
- Affirmed good: credentials are `import 'server-only'`, read lazily, never bundled to the browser; mirror tables are written only via the service-role admin client with RLS giving authenticated users read-only access; LWA refreshes coalesce concurrent requests and apply expiry skew.

### 4. Checklist to flip fake → real (ordered)

1. **Add `SELLER_ID`** to `AmazonConfig`/`REQUIRED_ENV`; pass it as `sellerId` in `searchCatalogItems` whenever `sellerSkus` is set.
2. **Carry the seller SKU from the request input** (`opts.sellerSkus`) into mapped `CatalogItem.sku`; stop scanning `identifiers` for type `SKU`.
3. **Add `details=true`** to the `getInventorySummaries` query.
4. **Add `nextToken` pagination loops** to catalog, inventory, and ads.
5. **Migrate Ads to SP v3:** `POST /sp/campaigns/list`, `application/vnd.spCampaign.v3+json` content-type/accept, JSON body, parse `{ campaigns, nextToken }`, read nested `budget.budget`, map uppercase state enum.
6. **Verify the reorder demand mirror against live credentials:** one `GET_LEDGER_SUMMARY_VIEW_DATA` report per marketplace+window on a sync/cron path; presigned-S3 gzip-TSV download with no SP-API auth header; parse to a SKU→daily-demand map persisted as a mirror; poll for `DONE`/`FATAL`/`CANCELLED`; page reads the mirror instead of making per-SKU calls.
7. **Supply prod credentials and flip flags:** real LWA creds + refresh tokens, `SELLER_ID`, `ADS_PROFILE_ID`; set `AMAZON_USE_SANDBOX=false`, `ADS_USE_SANDBOX=false`, `AMAZON_USE_FAKE=false`.
8. **Add proactive throttle + honor `Retry-After` / `x-amzn-RateLimit-Limit`** (FBA 2 rps, catalog/ads limits).
9. **Add a `User-Agent` header;** filter catalog summaries/images by active `marketplace.id` and prefer `variant === 'MAIN'`.
10. **[Polish] Drop the superfluous `Authorization: Bearer`** on SP-API requests.

Sources: [SP Products v2→v3 migration guide](https://advertising.amazon.com/API/docs/en-us/reference/migration-guides/sp-v2-v3), [Sponsored Products v3 OpenAPI](https://advertising.amazon.com/API/docs/en-us/sponsored-products/3-0/openapi/prod). SP-API Catalog Items v2022-04-01 and FBA Inventory v1 claims verified against developer-docs.amazon.com and the amzn/selling-partner-api-models OpenAPI in the supplied verification.
